title: arXiv 2610.13676: On the Encoding of Calendar Features in Covariate-Informed Time Series Foundation Models (abstract page)
note: Fetched. v1 submitted 9 Oct 2026, cs.LG, CC BY 4.0, seven authors. Abstract: seven calendar encodings (ordinal, one-hot, cyclic, four target encodings) compared across four foundation models on nine hourly datasets, zero-shot rolling evaluation; MASE differs by up to 9.9% on non-holidays and 83% on holidays within one model. No code link on the page.

title: arXiv 2610.13676v1 full text: setup
note: Fetched. Models: Chronos-2, TabPFN-TS-3, TiRex-2, TimesFM-3. Nine hourly series, one test year each: Madrid traffic, NYC subway and bus, TransnetBW control-area load (2025), three NetzeBW low-voltage feeders, Alicante water, DC bike rentals. Context 8192 h, horizon 24 h, stride 24 h, origin 00:00, fev 0.10.0, MASE and SQL scaled by 168 h seasonal naive. Holidays from the holidays library.

title: arXiv 2610.13676v1 full text: Table 2 and discussion
note: Fetched. Best-to-worst encoding gap in mean MASE within a model: non-holidays 4.8% (TiRex-2) to 9.9% (TabPFN-TS-3); holidays 44% (TabPFN-TS-3) to 83% (TiRex-2). Chronos-2 mean MASE: no covariates 0.6353 non-holiday, 2.2299 holiday; ordinal, one-hot and cyclic are worse than no covariates on non-holidays (0.6440, 0.6626, 0.6523); best is two target encodings (0.6218, 1.2285). No intervals or tests.

title: arXiv 2610.13676v1 full text: Table 7 (TransnetBW load)
note: Fetched. TransnetBW total load, Chronos-2 MASE: no covariates 0.4205 non-holiday and 2.3853 holiday; one-hot 0.4376 and 1.6213; ordinal 0.4162 and 0.7864; target encoding with holiday as Sunday 0.4109 and 0.5654. So on the one system-load series calendar inputs cut holiday error by up to about three quarters and move ordinary days by a few percent either way.

title: arXiv 2610.13676v1 full text: reproducibility, limits, appendix
note: Fetched. Code is promised on publication; no repository linked. Data are public. No pre-registration mentioned. Authors say no dataset is in the models pretraining data. Stated limits: hourly, calendar-driven targets only; no benefit expected where temperature drives the target; weather covariates left to future work. A context-2048 rerun (Table 14) shows the same pattern.

title: arXiv 2610.13676v1 full text: pipeline caveats
note: Fetched. All covariates are passed as numbers, so no model applies its own categorical handling by dtype. Two models still branch on values: TabPFN-TS-3 re-encodes low-cardinality columns and TiRex-2 skips scaling for binary columns. Target encodings are target means per calendar cell, recomputed from each window context, so they add no future information.

title: Research call, sources 1 and 2: the preprint itself
note: Research call (standard, LinkedIn excluded), task d89ceece. Its only support for the claim is the preprint: the 9.9% and 83% figures are the authors own. It found no repository, no pre-registration, no independent replication and no dispute. It notes there are no intervals for the holiday gap and that holiday windows are few in one test year.

title: Chronos-2: From Univariate to Universal Forecasting (research source 3)
note: Research call, source 3; not fetched in this run. The Chronos-2 paper: the model takes past-only and known-future covariates, real-valued or categorical, zero-shot, through group attention. Supports that the central model can accept calendar columns in either form; says nothing about which encoding is better.

title: TiRex-2: Generalizing TiRex to Multivariate Data and Streaming (research source 4)
note: Research call, source 4; not fetched in this run. The TiRex-2 paper: multivariate model with past and future-known covariates. Background on the model with the largest holiday gap in the preprint; not a test of calendar encodings.

title: A Calendar-Aware Frequency-Decoupled Framework for Day-Ahead Substation Load Forecasting (research source 5)
note: Research call, source 5; not fetched in this run. A supervised day-ahead substation load method in China that encodes weekday, weekend, holiday and make-up day as separate states instead of a binary flag. Different models and data; background only, not a replication.
